database.title: Where should this platform keep its data?
database.help: Asked first because nothing else can be stored until it is answered. This is the one choice here that cannot be changed later in Settings.
database.restartWarning: Choosing this restarts the platform so it can connect. It takes about twenty seconds, and this page waits for it. The passwords are generated for you and stored on the server — you never have to type them.

database.failed: The database could not be configured. Please try again.

postgres.name: PostgreSQL
postgres.note: Recommended. Runs one site or many, keeping each site's data separate at the database level.

sqlite.name: SQLite
sqlite.note: One file, no database server to run. This installation will only ever serve a single site — it has no way to keep two sites' data apart.

mysql.name: MySQL
mysql.note: A database server you already run. Keeps roles and backups like PostgreSQL, but has no way to keep two sites' data apart — so this installation will only ever serve a single site. Not included in this stack: point it at your own server.

database.ownerRoleHelp: This driver keeps each site's data separate, which needs two roles: one that owns the tables and runs migrations, and one that serves requests and owns nothing. Serving requests as the owner turns that separation off without any error. Both must already exist on your server.

domain.title: The admin's domain
domain.adminUrlHelp: Prefilled with whatever you are using right now — a bare IP is fine until DNS is ready. This is what the platform routes the admin by, so change it only if you will reach it somewhere else, and point that domain here first.
domain.unclaimedWarning: This installation has not been claimed yet. Until you finish, anyone who can reach it can set it up instead of you. It stops accepting setup 15 minutes after starting.

infrastructure.theMostOneSiteMay: The most one site may store in themes it uploaded itself, all of them together. Every site's uploads share one volume on this server, so this protects the other sites. A theme being replaced does not count twice.
infrastructure.howManyOfItsOwn: How many of its own themes a site may keep. Themes the platform assigns to a site do not count.

When on, a site's admin can upload a plugin that runs only for that site, in its own process under its own user, with no database schema, network, admin screens or install step. The server must isolate plugin identity; where it cannot, sites are told uploads are unavailable.

infrastructure.theMostOneSiteMay2: The most one site may store in plugins it uploaded, all of them together. An upload larger than this is refused while it streams.
infrastructure.howManyOfItsOwn2: How many of its own plugins a site may keep. Plugins the platform offers to sites do not count.

infrastructure.failedToSaveTheServer: Failed to save the server rendering cap.
infrastructure.pluginIsolationSettingsSavedThe: Plugin isolation settings saved. The limits apply to every running plugin now. Where plugins run changes for plugins already loaded when the API restarts — use the button under "Where plugins run".

infrastructure.failedToSaveThePlugin: Failed to save the plugin isolation settings.
infrastructure.theApiExitsInMs: The API exits in {{exitInMs}}ms and its supervisor starts it again. It is unavailable until then.
infrastructure.theApiCouldNotBe: The API could not be restarted.
infrastructure.notSetAutomaticCertificatesAre: Not set — automatic certificates are off
infrastructure.thePlatformCanNowObtain: The platform can now obtain certificates for hosts set to Automatic.
infrastructure.automaticCertificatesStayOffUntil: Automatic certificates stay off until both an authority and a platform address are set.
infrastructure.couldNotSaveTheCertificate: Could not save the certificate settings.
infrastructure.leaveTheseBlankAndThe: Leave these blank and the platform never obtains a certificate itself — hosts keep whatever was uploaded.
infrastructure.pickTheStagingAuthorityTo: Pick the staging authority to test the whole flow without spending a production rate limit. Its certificates are not trusted by browsers.
infrastructure.optionalUsedForAccountNotices: Optional. Used for account notices only — expiry warnings come from this platform, not from the authority.
infrastructure.onePerLineTheseAre: One per line. These are printed as the DNS instructions a customer follows, and a domain is checked against them before any certificate is ordered — so a wrong value here sends people to the wrong machine. The record must point straight at these addresses, not through a proxy or CDN; a proxied host can only use an uploaded certificate.
infrastructure.savedLeaveBlankToKeep: Saved — leave blank to keep, or use Clear to remove
infrastructure.noTokenIsSavedWildcard: No token is saved — wildcard issuance is off.
infrastructure.resolvedFromThisPlatformS: Resolved from this platform’s own hostnames, just now
infrastructure.ifThoseHostnamesSitBehind: If those hostnames sit behind a proxy or CDN this is the proxy’s address, not this machine’s. Check before using it.
infrastructure.restrictsFrontendAccessWhileYou: Restricts frontend access while you work on the instance.
infrastructure.howManyDistinctThemePlugin: How many distinct theme + plugin sets the storefront keeps loaded at once, each in its own render process; sites on the same set share one. Beyond this, the least recently used is stopped and rebuilt on demand.
infrastructure.aThemeWorldThatAllocates: A theme world that allocates past this is killed; the storefront answers that request without server rendering and starts a fresh process on the next one.
infrastructure.aPageRenderThatDoes: A page render that does not finish within this is abandoned and its process restarted; the page is served for client-side rendering instead.
infrastructure.isolatedEachActivePluginRuns: Isolated: each active plugin runs in its own process — it cannot read the platform's secrets, every database call is bound to the request's site, and it has a memory ceiling and a deadline. Shared: inside the API process. Plugins that declare sandbox: false stay shared either way. A plugin installed from now on follows this at once; plugins already loaded move when the API restarts.
infrastructure.savedPluginsAlreadyLoadedStill: Saved. Plugins already loaded still run where they were until the API restarts.

restart.apiDescription: Exits the API process; the container supervisor starts it again. Reloads plugin code, manifests and settings from disk. Requests in flight are dropped.
restart.apiWarning: The admin and the storefront both depend on the API, so both stop working until it is back.
restart.adminDescription: Exits the admin process; the container supervisor starts it again. Clears this app's server-side caches.
restart.adminWarning: This is the app you are using right now. This page will stop responding until the admin is back — reload it then.
restart.frontendDescription: Exits the storefront process; the container supervisor starts it again. Clears its rendering caches and re-reads theme and plugin bundles.
restart.frontendWarning: Visitors will get an error until the storefront is back.
restart.otherDescription: Exits the process; the container supervisor starts it again.

infrastructure.theDeployCapacityCouldNot: The deploy capacity could not be read.

infrastructure.eitherModeAReleaseWith: Either mode: a release with new database migrations always restarts (the old version cannot keep serving a changed schema), and the gateway itself restarts for a second or two.
infrastructure.howAReleaseReplacesThe: How a release replaces the running apps
infrastructure.restartEveryAppIsRecreated: Restart: every app is recreated at once, and every site is down for about 45 seconds. Rolling: one app at a time, the new copy serving before the old one stops — no downtime, but it needs spare memory for a second copy of the largest app while it is swapped. Plugin processes run in the extension-host and carry over either way; a rolling deploy leaves the extension-host itself on its version, and it moves to a new one on the next restart deploy.

infrastructure.theAppExitsInMs: The {{app}} app exits in {{exitInMs}}ms and its supervisor starts it again. It is unavailable until then.

infrastructure.unavailableThisInstallHasNo: Unavailable: this install has no URL configured for the {{app}} app.
infrastructure.dnsTokenHint: Needed only to order a WILDCARD certificate (*.example.com) — that can only be proven through DNS, never HTTP. Leave it blank and every host keeps ordering the single-name HTTP-01 certificate above. The token needs Zone → DNS → Edit on the zone it will manage; it is stored encrypted and is never shown again once saved.
infrastructure.auditTrailNotLog: This is not the log above. It removes the audit trail — security denials, settings changes, MCP tool calls and AI invocations — for every site on this platform.
infrastructure.auditMinimum: Minimum 180 days. This journal is this platform’s EU AI Act Art. 12 record, which is expected to survive six months; a shorter window is refused rather than quietly shortened. Blank — keep forever — is always allowed.
infrastructure.rollingFits: This server has room for a rolling deploy.
infrastructure.rollingWillRestart: Not enough memory for a rolling deploy right now — deploys will restart instead.
infrastructure.rollingNoRoom: Not enough memory for a rolling deploy right now.

security.howManyFailedSignIns: How many failed sign-ins for the same email and IP lock that combination out.
security.failuresMoreThanThisFar: Failures more than this far apart do not add up; the counter restarts instead of reaching the threshold.
security.howLongALockedEmail: How long a locked email and IP combination is refused, even with the correct password.
security.onceTheCaptchaThresholdBelow: Once the captcha threshold below is reached, the sign-in request must carry a captcha answer before the password is even checked.
security.onlyUsedWhileTheCaptcha: Only used while the captcha requirement above is on. Keep it below the lockout threshold or the account locks first.
security.howLongAUserStays: How long a user stays logged in before re-authentication is required. Applies to the next sign-in; sessions already issued keep the lifetime they were given.
security.addAnExtraLayerOf: Add an extra layer of security to administrative accounts. Turning this off blocks new enrolment; users who already enrolled keep their second factor.
security.emailTheAccountOwnerWhen: Email the account owner when a password changes, a two-factor method is added or removed, or a sign-in looks unusual. Off means those emails are not sent at all.
security.theMaximumNumberOfRequests: The maximum number of requests a single anonymous IP can make in one window.
security.theMaximumNumberOfRequests2: The maximum number of requests a signed-in session can make. Counted per IP plus token, so one busy admin session cannot starve another behind the same IP.
security.theMaximumNumberOfRequests3: The maximum number of requests an internal service can make. Counted per calling service address, so the storefront renderer, which fetches this API several times per page view from a single container, does not spend the anonymous visitor budget.
security.addressesOrCidrBlocksYour: Addresses or CIDR blocks your own services call this API from, comma separated (for example 172.16.0.0/12). A caller is internal only when both its network hop and its resolved address are listed, never because of a header it sent. Leave empty and nothing is internal: every anonymous caller falls back to the per-IP limit above.
security.everyCounterAboveResetsAfter: Every counter above resets after this window elapses. Example: 60000 is one minute. Fixed-window: a caller who trips a limit is locked out for up to this long, so keep it short. Changing it restarts the counters.
security.shorterPasswordsAreRejectedWhen: Shorter passwords are rejected when an account is created, changed or reset. Existing passwords are not revoked.
security.aNewPasswordMustContain: A new password must contain at least one A-Z character.
security.aNewPasswordMustContain2: A new password must contain at least one a-z character.
security.aNewPasswordMustContain3: A new password must contain at least one digit.
security.aNewPasswordMustContain4: A new password must contain at least one character that is not a letter or a digit.
security.howManyOfAUser: How many of a user's previous passwords are refused when they choose a new one. Set to 0 to allow reuse.
security.askABreachCheckProvider: Ask a breach-check provider whether a chosen password appears in a public breach corpus. This calls the "auth:password:breach-check" hook. With no plugin answering it, nothing is rejected.
security.howLongAPasswordReset: How long a password-reset link works before the user has to request a new one.
security.howLongTheConfirmationLink: How long the confirmation link sent to a new email address stays valid.
security.residentSetOfTheApi: Resident set of the api process
security.pluginProcessesAreSeparateEach: Plugin processes are separate: each carries its own limit, listed below.
security.noPluginIsRunningIn: No plugin is running in its own process right now.
security.apiProtectionAndAccountDefense: API protection and account defense synced.
security.securitySettingsCouldNotBe: Security settings could not be loaded
security.securityStatisticsCouldNotBe: Security statistics could not be loaded
security.passwordPolicyLoginProtectionRate: Password policy, login protection, rate limits and the audit trail are stored per site. Choose a site from the site menu to configure its security.
security.physicalTableNamesCommaSeparated: Physical table names, comma separated. Plugin database writes to these tables are not recorded in the audit log — meant for high-volume telemetry tables whose per-row writes would drown the trail. Clear it and every plugin write is audited. Applies within a minute of saving.
